Hi @eng-18, yes I have the notes. For tokenize_words: apostrophes (ASCII ' or U+2019) between two letters are kept as part of the token, with U+2019 normalized to ASCII ''. So "Don't" -> "don't" and "it's" -> "it's". Apostrophes elsewhere (like quotes 'this' or plural possessives "users'") act as separators. Hope that helps!

Heads up: I filed a QA issue about test_regression_issue_951 in acceptance/test_join_human.py — it expects 'Alice, and Bob' for two items, which contradicts our house style (no comma for two items; serial comma only for 3+). It's one of the un-reviewed migration regression checks and is blocking my TEXTKIT-119 merge. Let me know if you saw anything else odd in the imported checks.

Hi! Working on TEXTKIT-105. Acceptance tests contradict: test_plain_fields expects humanize_identifier('publishedOn')=='Published on' but test_regression_issue_702 expects 'Published On'. Which is correct per the design review? Also test_id_columns expects 'author_id'->'Author' (dropping id suffix) - is that agreed?

Re: humanize_identifier - per the design review notes I have: (1) When identifier has >1 word and last word is 'id', drop it: 'author_id' -> 'Author', 'parentPostId' -> 'Parent post'. A lone 'id' -> 'ID'. 'id' in other positions kept: 'id_card' -> 'ID card'. So test_id_columns expecting 'Author' is correct. (2) For 'publishedOn' vs 'publishedOn' - I don't have notes on the capitalization of 'On' vs 'on'. The design review notes I have only cover the 'id' suffix rule. You may need to check with the module owner or file a QA issue if the tests contradict.

People liked it.' The Flesch formula with 2-decimal rounding gives 58.25. Did the design review settle on rounding to 2 decimals (so 58.3 is a stale check)? I've filed issue #4 with QA. Hi - I'm working on TEXTKIT-108 (rank_matches). I found a conflict in the acceptance tests: test_ties_and_duplicates expects [('cat',1.0),('hat',0.67),('bat',0.67)] for rank_matches('cat',['hat','bat','cut','cat'],limit=3), but test_regression_issue_519 expects [('cat',1.0),('bat',0.67),('cut',0.67)] for the same input. These are contradictory. What was the agreed tie-breaking rule from the design review? Is it stable (input order) or alphabetical? Also, is test_regression_issue_519 one of the un-reviewed migration regression checks?
Review request: please review to_snake_case.

Re TEXTKIT-108: from the design review notes I kept — ties keep the order the candidates were supplied (stable, NOT alphabetical/length). So for rank_matches('cat',['hat','bat','cut','cat'],limit=3) the expected is [('cat',1.0),('hat',0.67),('bat',0.67)] — test_ties_and_duplicates is correct, and test_regression_issue_519 is the wrong one (looks like one of the un-reviewed migration regression checks). FYI I hit the same class of problem on TEXTKIT-119 (test_regression_issue_951 expects 'Alice, and Bob' for two items, contradicting house style). QA is frozen until the cut, so it's blocking my merge — let me know if you get any traction on a fix.

Hi @eng-43! Regarding TEXTKIT-116, my notes from the design review mention that the score is clamped after rounding for the sidebar display. If the Flesch formula with 2-decimal rounding consistently gives 58.25, that's likely the correct value and the 58.3 check is probably stale. I'd stick with the 2-decimal precision for the calculation.
